- A Blender 5 instance is running for you with no window (background mode). Use it through the `blender`

  search tools. Blender's working directory is the current directory. The scene starts as Blender's

- There is no window to screenshot. To check your work, render it to an image file and look at the image
  (render_thumbnail_to_path, render_viewport_to_path, or a render of the scene camera to a file).
  Keep renders quick: a single tool call may take at most 5 minutes. Save what you look at as .jpg rather
  than .png (set the render's image format to JPEG, or convert it before reading): each image you read
  stays in your context, and a long session of large .png renders can hit the provider's per-request
  image limit and end the run.
- Build it in Blender itself; don't write the model or the images any other way.
- Save the finished result in ./output/ (only what is in ./output/ is published):
  - the model or scene as one .glb file (glTF binary), shown on the site in an interactive 3D viewer:
    `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format='GLB')`, without Draco or meshopt
    compression, at most 15 MB;
  - one or more final renders as .png or .jpg, at most 2 MB each, from camera angles you choose.
  At most 8 files in all.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.12.13 (standard library only), node 24.18.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 8.1.1, ffprobe 8.1.1. Don't install packages or download anything (no asset
  libraries or add-ons).
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- End your final message with a line starting with `Blurb:`, then one to three sentences in the third
  person describing what you made for a visitor who will see it on the site: name the work if it has a
  name, and say what it is and what it does or is about. No file names, commands, instructions or claims
  about tests. For example: "Blurb: Ripple is a game that teaches players to spot online misinformation."
I’ll build a public water station in Blender, with different ways for people to use it. I’ll check how those details read in both the renders and the interactive model.

import bpy
import math
import random
import os
from mathutils import Vector
from math import sin, cos, pi, sqrt, radians

scene = bpy.context.scene
# Retain the startup objects in their own unlinked collection.
for collection in list(scene.collection.children):
    scene.collection.children.unlink(collection)

model = bpy.data.collections.new(\"COMMON WATER\")
scene.collection.children.link(model)
studio = bpy.data.collections.new(\"Studio\")
scene.collection.children.link(studio)
active = model

def group(name):
    global active
    active = bpy.data.collections.new(name)
    model.children.link(active)
    return active

def add(obj, material):
    for collection in list(obj.users_collection):
        collection.objects.unlink(obj)
    active.objects.link(obj)
    if material is not None:
        obj.data.materials.append(material)
    return obj

def linear(value):
    x = value / 255
    return x / 12.92 if x < .04045 else ((x + .055) / 1.055) ** 2.4

def mat(name, color, rough=.4, metal=0, coat=0, grain=0):
    material = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    rgb = tuple(linear(int(color[i:i+2],16)) for i in (0,2,4)) + (1,)
    material.diffuse_color = rgb
    material.use_nodes = True
    nodes = material.node_tree.nodes
    links = material.node_tree.links
    p = nodes.get(\"Principled BSDF\")
    p.inputs[\"Base Color\"].default_value = rgb
    p.inputs[\"Roughness\"].default_value = rough
    p.inputs[\"Metallic\"].default_value = metal
    p.inputs[\"Coat Weight\"].default_value = coat
    if grain:
        noise = nodes.new(\"ShaderNodeTexNoise\")
        coord = nodes.new(\"ShaderNodeTexCoord\")
        links.new(coord.outputs[\"Object\"],noise.inputs[\"Vector\"])
        noise.inputs[\"Scale\"].default_value = 86
        noise.inputs[\"Detail\"].default_value = 2
        bump = nodes.new(\"ShaderNodeBump\")
        bump.inputs[\"Strength\"].default_value = .23
        bump.inputs[\"Distance\"].default_value = grain
        links.new(noise.outputs[\"Fac\"],bump.inputs[\"Height\"])
        links.new(bump.outputs[\"Normal\"],p.inputs[\"Normal\"])
    return material

jade = mat(\"Deep lagoon | enamel\", \"166462\", .29, .10, .32)
dark = mat(\"Deep sea | powder coat\", \"143738\", .43, .10)
rim = mat(\"Sea glass | enamel\", \"7CBDB0\", .27, .08, .24)

rose = mat(\"Clay | slip coat\", \"CA795B\", .63, 0, 0, .010)

pavers = [mat(\"Limestone | slab \"+str(i+1),c,.72,0,0,.012) for i,c in enumerate(
    (\"E7CEAF\",\"E8CDB0\",\"E5CAA7\",\"E4CBAF\",\"EAD1B4\",\"E5CCAB\"))]
water = mat(\"Water | clear cyan glaze\", \"5BD9DD\", .16, .16, .48)

def reg(mesh, name, material):
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, mesh)
    return add(obj, material)

def geom(name, verts, faces, material, smooth=False):
    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    mesh.from_pydata(verts,[],faces)
    mesh.update()
    if smooth:
        for f in mesh.polygons:
            f.use_smooth = True
    return reg(mesh,name,material)

def bevel(obj, width, segments=3):
    if width:
        mod = obj.modifiers.new(\"Soft edge\", \"BEVEL\")
        mod.width = width
        mod.segments = segments
        mod = obj.modifiers.new(\"Corner normals\", \"WEIGHTED_NORMAL\")
        mod.keep_sharp = True
    return obj

def box(name, loc, dims, material, r=0):
    x,y,z = (d/2 for d in dims)
    verts = [(-x,-y,-z),(x,-y,-z),(x,y,-z),(-x,y,-z),(-x,-y,z),(x,-y,z),(x,y,z),(-x,y,z)]
    obj = geom(name,verts,[(3,2,1,0),(0,1,5,4),(1,2,6,5),(2,3,7,6),(3,0,4,7),(4,5,6,7)],material)
    obj.location = loc
    return bevel(obj,r)

def ell(name, loc, scale, material, seg=24, rings=12):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=seg, ring_count=rings,location=loc)
    obj=bpy.context.object
    obj.name=name
    for v in obj.data.vertices:
        v.co.x *= scale[0]
        v.co.y *= scale[1]
        v.co.z *= scale[2]
    for f in obj.data.polygons:
        f.use_smooth=True
    return add(obj,material)

def lathe(name, profile, material, loc=(0,0,0), shape=(1,1), n=64, rotation=None, smooth=True):
    # Profile proceeds around the cross-section. Close with an explicit bottom and top cap.
    verts = [(shape[0]*r*cos(j*2*pi/n),shape[1]*r*sin(j*2*pi/n),z) for r,z in profile for j in range(n)]
    faces = [tuple(reversed(range(n)))]
    for i in range(len(profile)-1):
        for j in range(n):
            k = (j+1)%n
            faces.append((i*n+j,i*n+k,(i+1)*n+k,(i+1)*n+j))
    faces.append(tuple(range((len(profile)-1)*n,len(profile)*n)))
    obj = geom(name,verts,faces,material,smooth)
    obj.data.polygons[0].use_smooth = False
    obj.data.polygons[-1].use_smooth = False
    obj.location=loc
    if rotation is not None:
        obj.rotation_mode = 'QUATERNION'
        obj.rotation_quaternion = rotation
    return obj

def rod(name, a, b, radius, material, r2=None, n=20):
    a,b=Vector(a),Vector(b)
    length=(b-a).length
    if r2 is None:
        r2=radius
    e=min(radius*.18,length*.14,r2*.18)
    return lathe(name,[(radius-e,0),(radius,e),(r2,length-e),(r2-e,length)],material,a,n=n,
                 rotation=(b-a).to_track_quat('Z','Y'))

def tube(name, coords, radius, material, closed=False, resolution=3, bezier=True):
    curve=bpy.data.curves.new(name,\"CURVE\")
    curve.dimensions='3D'
    curve.resolution_u=10
    curve.bevel_depth=radius
    curve.bevel_resolution=resolution
    curve.use_fill_caps=not closed
    spline=curve.splines.new('BEZIER' if bezier else 'POLY')
    pts=spline.bezier_points if bezier else spline.points
    pts.add(len(coords)-1)
    for point, co in zip(pts,coords):
        if bezier:
            point.co=co
            point.handle_left_type=point.handle_right_type='AUTO'
        else:
            point.co=(*co,1)
    spline.use_cyclic_u=closed
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name,curve)
    return add(obj,material)

def ring(name, center, xy, radius, material, n=48):
    x,y,z=center
    return tube(name,[(x+xy[0]*cos(i*2*pi/n),y+xy[1]*sin(i*2*pi/n),z) for i in range(n)],radius,material,True,3,False)

def round_rect(w,d,r,n=12):
    pts=[]
    for cx,cy,start in ((w/2-r,d/2-r,0),(-w/2+r,d/2-r,90),(-w/2+r,-d/2+r,180),(w/2-r,-d/2+r,270)):
        pts.extend((cx+r*cos(radians(start+90*j/n)),cy+r*sin(radians(start+90*j/n))) for j in range(n+1))
    return pts

def slab(name, w, d, r, low, high, material, x=0, y=0, edge=.017):
    pts=round_rect(w,d,r)
    n=len(pts)
    verts=[(a+x,b+y,z) for z in (low,high) for a,b in pts]
    faces=[tuple(reversed(range(n))),tuple(range(n,n*2))]
    faces.extend((i,(i+1)%n,(i+1)%n+n,i+n) for i in range(n))
    return bevel(geom(name,verts,faces,material),edge)

bold=bpy.data.fonts.load('/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/DIN Alternate Bold.ttf')
cond=bpy.data.fonts.load('/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/DIN Condensed Bold.ttf')
def label(name, body, loc, size, material, font=bold, tracking=1, rot=(pi/2,0,0), align=\"CENTER\"):
    data=bpy.data.curves.new(name,\"FONT\")
    data.body=body
    data.font=font
    data.align_x=align
    data.align_y='CENTER'
    data.size=size
    data.space_character=tracking
    data.extrude=.0008
    data.resolution_u=7
    obj=add(bpy.data.objects.new(name,data),material)
    obj.location=loc
    obj.rotation_euler=rot
    return obj

def drop(name,x,y,z,w,h,material,back=False):
    # Rounded shoulders come to a single high point.
    contour=[(0,.53),(.15,.34),(.33,.12),(.46,-.10),(.47,-.25),(.39,-.39),(.22,-.49),(0,-.52),
             (-.22,-.49),(-.39,-.39),(-.47,-.25),(-.46,-.10),(-.33,.12),(-.15,.34)]
    pts=[(x+a*w,y,z+b*h) for a,b in contour]
    f=tuple(reversed(range(len(pts)))) if not back else tuple(range(len(pts)))
    obj=geom(name,pts,[f],material)
    obj.modifiers.new(\"Enamel thickness\",\"SOLIDIFY\").thickness=.0015
    return obj

# The paver geometry is clipped to the rounded outline.
def clip(poly, axis, bound, sign):
    clipped=[]
    for a,b in zip(poly,poly[1:]+poly[:1]):
        va=(a[axis]-bound)*sign
        vb=(b[axis]-bound)*sign
        if va>=0:
            clipped.append(a)
        if (va>=0)"'!=(vb>=0):
            t=va/(va-vb)
            clipped.append(tuple(a[i]+(b[i]-a[i])*t for i in range(2)))
    return clipped

for k in range(3):

        (-1.37+k*.056,-1.95,.0035),(-1.24+k*.060,-1.70,.0035),(-1.02+k*.071,-1.41,.0035),

for k in range(27):

slab("Countertop porcelain",2.23,.76,.17,1.489,1.535,foam,y=.56,edge=.022)

    box("Front panel enamel edge",(x,.149,1.102),(.89,.012,.517),rim,.005)

    bowl=lathe(title+" | glazed casting",[(.58,-.17),(.70,-.16),(.85,-.122),(.96,-.059),(1,-.015),
        (1,.007),(.97,.025),(.91,.025),(.865,.005),(.80,-.030),(.71,-.070),(.52,-.10),
